title: qos_contention 10000ms.png is byte-identical to 01000ms.png — the demo's third T2 capture pins no additional state
evidence: sha256sum: 'c7a895a2b6bc32b57c14c958ee6722af3b1ad9371639ff66c0b7bc22adc42702  goldens/qos_contention/01000ms.png' and 'c7a895a2b6bc32b57c14c958ee6722af3b1ad9371639ff66c0b7bc22adc42702  goldens/qos_contention/10000ms.png'; c5.patch lists BOTH as 'new file mode 100644 / index 0000000..3c26f46' (identical blobs), while 03000ms.png is 'index 0000000..42d495d'; pixel diff 01000 vs 03000 = 'diff pixels: 421 bbox: (413, 353, 809, 366)'.
detail: The 10s capture is a genuine steady-state artifact, not a copy: the pixel-exact T2 gate (compare_images, mismatch>0 fails) passes it at tick 200, and the 25ms period-5 spawn cycle makes tick 20 == tick 200 visually (queue full from tick 17; 334 E9 drops). The third capture is a redundant duplicate — the golden set pins only 2 distinct frames.
recommended_fix: Drop the 10000ms capture from qos_contention.dem or move it to a pre-steady-state moment (e.g. 600ms) so the third capture pins a non-duplicate frame; re-bless deliberately.
